messages:
Maya N.: Heads up — saw errors from the JS SDK when running inside Vercel Edge middleware. Auth retries blow up with `TypeError: crypto.subtle is not a function` and then fetch gets into a weird retry loop :thinking_face:

Eli K.: Hmm. Is that the edge build or local dev?

Maya N.: Edge build on Vercel (Next.js middleware). Local edge emulation also reproduces. Happens when SDK tries to compute HMAC for auth and then also when it re-issues a request on 401.

Chris P.: That makes sense — Vercel edge is sandboxed and uses Web Crypto, but some bundlers or polyfills swap Node globals so code that expects `crypto.subtle` or `TextEncoder` can fail. Any stacktrace?

Maya N.: Short one: `at auth.signRequest (node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/node/auth.js:45:12)` then `TypeError: crypto.subtle is not a function` followed by fetch throwing and retry logic hitting `clone()` on a Response which isn't supported the same way in the runtime.

Samir R.: Two separate things: (1) crypto availability (HMAC vs webcrypto differences) and (2) response cloning / body stream semantics in middleware. We should avoid Node-specific entrypoint in edge bundles and provide an edge-first export.

Eli K.: Agreed. Workarounds we've seen: polyfill WebCrypto in the bundle, or offer a tiny edge-compatible auth implementation that uses globalThis.crypto.subtle. Polyfills get messy with Next's Edge bundling though.

Maya N.: Can we add an official note to SDK docs and a minimal fix in the middleware adapter? Example workaround that worked locally for me:

```js
// middleware/edge-auth-shim.js
if (typeof globalThis.crypto === 'undefined' && typeof self !== 'undefined' && self.crypto) {
  globalThis.crypto = self.crypto;
}
if (typeof TextEncoder === 'undefined') {
  // lightweight polyfill for encoders used by HMAC
  globalThis.TextEncoder = require('util').TextEncoder;
}
```

Maya N.: After that the HMAC step ran, but I still saw retry fallout — fetch retry tried to re-read a streamed body.

Chris P.: For retries in edge middleware we should avoid cloning streamed request/response bodies. SDK retry logic must detect e.g. `Request.bodyUsed` or prefer non-streaming retry-friendly APIs. Alternatively, provide a config flag `edgeRetryMode: true` that changes behavior.

Samir R.: We can add an `exports` entry so bundlers pick the right entry: example snippet for package.json conditional exports (edge-first):

```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "default": "./dist/node/index.cjs"
}
```

Samir R.: That plus an `edge` build that doesn't pull in node-only crypto or node-fetch should greatly reduce breakage.

Eli K.: TS types note: when we ship edge entrypoints we should add an `types` field per entry or include a small `index.d.ts` at `./dist/edge/index.d.ts` with DOM libs so devs don't need to add `lib: ["dom", "es2021"]` hacks. Document that in DX onboarding.

Maya N.: Sounds good. For short-term docs/FAQ I'll add the shim snippet and recommend turning off automatic retries in middleware (or using `edgeRetryMode`) until an SDK patch lands.

devex-bot: Created a GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/452 for "Edge middleware: sandboxed globals & retry semantics" and assigned to @samir.

Chris P.: Flagging potential user-facing note for Release Notes: "Edge: improved compatibility for Vercel/Next.js middleware; added edge-specific entrypoint and retry mode."

Samir R.: I'll start a branch with the conditional exports + small shim and a test that runs under `vercel dev` emulation. Will ping when ready for review.

Maya N.: Thanks — will update the docs page and add the workaround to the Next.js example app. :+1:
